name: ifconfig
summary: Shows and configures network interfaces (older tool).
description: The historic tool from the net-tools package, still very common in courses and tutorials. It is no longer installed by default on recent distributions: its replacement is ip (ifconfig corresponds to ip a). Without an argument, it shows the active interfaces with their IPv4, IPv6 and MAC addresses.

options.description: Shows every interface, including disabled ones.

example.output:
Iface   MTU    RX-OK RX-ERR TX-OK TX-ERR Flg
wlp2s0  1500  182734      0 90211      0 BMRU

arguments.name: INTERFACE
arguments.description: Interface to show or configure: eth0, wlan0, lo…

arguments.name: SETTINGS
arguments.description: up, down, an IP address, netmask 255.255.255.0…

examples.explanation: The active interfaces and their addresses.
examples.output:
wlp2s0: flags=4163<UP,BROADCAST,RUNNING,MULTICAST>  mtu 1500
        inet 192.168.1.42  netmask 255.255.255.0  broadcast 192.168.1.255
        ether 3c:a9:f4:12:ab:cd  txqueuelen 1000  (Ethernet)

examples.explanation: Gives eth0 an address and brings it up (modern equivalent: ip addr add).

dangerNote: Disabling or reconfiguring the interface you are connected through over SSH cuts the connection.
